The average treatment effect is about **4.18**, estimated by regressing the outcome `y` on the treatment indicator and all 25 covariates (x1–x25) in ordinary least squares. The coefficient on `treatment` is 4.1765 (standard error 0.155).

The estimate depends on the method, so here are the alternatives I computed:

| Method | ATE estimate |
|---|---|
| Naive difference in means | 4.23 |
| OLS with covariates (reported) | 4.18 |
| Inverse-probability weighting (logit propensity) | 4.19 |
| G-computation (separate outcome models per arm) | 4.22 |

All of them put the effect around 4.2. I took the covariate-adjusted OLS coefficient as the answer because it is the most standard reading of "ATE" for this dataset.

ANSWER: 4.18
